sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: In March 2020, a few weeks after COVID-19 lockdowns began in the U.S.,
sentences.zh: 2020年3月，也就是美国开始新冠疫情封锁几周后，

sentences.en: we asked listeners to send us voice memos about their experiences of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 我们请听众发来语音备忘录，分享他们对疫情的亲身经历。

sentences.en: We recently went back and listened to those messages,
sentences.zh: 最近我们回过头来重听了这些留言，

sentences.en: each one a tiny time capsule of life in a world under lockdown.
sentences.zh: 每一条都是封锁世界中生活的微型时间胶囊。

sentences.en: Listeners told us about the stress of trying to find toilet paper and masks.
sentences.zh: 听众们向我们讲述了抢购卫生纸和口罩的压力。

sentences.en: They talked about the challenge of trying to work over Zoom,
sentences.zh: 他们谈到了通过Zoom远程办公的挑战，

sentences.en: and more than anything, they grappled with the sudden, shocking ways
sentences.zh: 而最重要的是，他们都在努力应对生活突然变得狭窄、孤立，

sentences.en: in which their lives had become smaller and more isolated.
sentences.zh: 那种令人震惊的转变。

sentences.en: I don't know if I could live with myself if I was stuck here
sentences.zh: 我不知道如果我被困在这里，

sentences.en: and something were to happen to my grandma.
sentences.zh: 而我奶奶出了什么事，我该如何面对自己。

sentences.en: And this is especially apparent when I found out that I could not visit my father
sentences.zh: 当我发现我无法去探望住在独立生活设施里的父亲时，

sentences.en: in his independent living facility.
sentences.zh: 这种感觉尤为明显。

sentences.en: My older sister gave birth to her son.
sentences.zh: 我姐姐生了个儿子。

sentences.en: We weren't able to be with her at the hospital,
sentences.zh: 我们没能去医院陪她，

sentences.en: nor have we been able to see him.
sentences.zh: 也没能见到那个孩子。

sentences.en: In those early days of the pandemic, so many of us found ourselves dreaming about what it would be like
sentences.zh: 在疫情初期的那些日子里，我们许多人都曾幻想过，

sentences.en: when we could once again hug friends and family outside our immediate household.
sentences.zh: 当我们可以再次拥抱核心家庭以外的朋友和亲人时，会是什么样子。

sentences.en: We fantasized about the moment when we could enjoy going out to a restaurant or a music venue.
sentences.zh: 我们幻想过能够再次享受外出就餐或去音乐场所的时刻。

sentences.en: We told ourselves that we would not take those moments for granted once we had them back.
sentences.zh: 我们告诉自己，一旦重新拥有这些时刻，绝不会将其视为理所当然。

sentences.en: And indeed, the first time I got to see relatives overseas and enjoy dinner out with friends,
sentences.zh: 确实，当我第一次见到海外的亲戚并和朋友们外出共进晚餐时，

sentences.en: it was truly amazing.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉真是太棒了。

sentences.en: The second time was pretty great as well.
sentences.zh: 第二次感觉也相当不错。

sentences.en: But after a while, that magical feeling inevitably started to fade,
sentences.zh: 但过了一段时间，那种神奇的感觉不可避免地开始消退，

sentences.en: no matter how hard I tried to hold on to it.
sentences.zh: 无论我多么努力地想要留住它。

sentences.en: We see this in many dimensions of our lives.
sentences.zh: 我们在生活的许多方面都看到了这一点。

sentences.en: So many love stories end at the point at which great romantic quests are consummated.
sentences.zh: 太多的爱情故事在浪漫的追求达成时就结束了。

sentences.en: Stories that follow lovers past the wedding day,
sentences.zh: 那些讲述恋人在婚礼之后，

sentences.en: into the years and decades of their marriages,
sentences.zh: 进入婚姻生活数年乃至数十年的故事，

sentences.en: those tend not to be romantic comedies.
sentences.zh: 往往不再是浪漫喜剧了。

sentences.en: It's easy to be cynical and say that nothing lasts, that everything fades away.
sentences.zh: 愤世嫉俗地说“没有什么能持久，一切都会消逝”很容易。

sentences.en: But this belies what actually happens in our minds as we experience triumphs and setbacks.
sentences.zh: 但这掩盖了我们在经历成功与挫折时，内心真实发生的变化。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain,
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》，

sentences.en: the psychology of habituation.
sentences.zh: 探讨习惯化的心理学。

sentences.en: How we get used to both the good and the bad in our lives
sentences.zh: 我们如何习惯生活中的好与坏，

sentences.en: and the surprising implications it has for happiness.
sentences.zh: 以及它对幸福感产生的惊人影响。

sentences.en: Think about the last time you saw one of your favorite desserts on a menu.
sentences.zh: 回想一下你上次在菜单上看到自己最喜欢的甜点时的情景。

sentences.en: Maybe it's the restaurant's signature chocolate cake.
sentences.zh: 也许那是餐厅的招牌巧克力蛋糕。

sentences.en: Your mouth waters as you read the description and you order a slice,
sentences.zh: 当你读到描述时，口水直流，于是点了一块，

sentences.en: gleefully anticipating how good it will taste.
sentences.zh: 满心欢喜地期待着它会有多美味。

sentences.en: The first bite does not disappoint.
sentences.zh: 第一口确实没让人失望。

sentences.en: It's out of this world.
sentences.zh: 简直是人间美味。

sentences.en: As you continue to dig in, however, something funny happens.
sentences.zh: 然而，当你继续吃的时候，有趣的事情发生了。

sentences.en: The cake no longer blows your mind.
sentences.zh: 蛋糕不再让你感到惊艳了。

sentences.en: You lift your fork to your mouth a few more times,
sentences.zh: 你又往嘴里送了几次叉子，

sentences.en: trying to recapture the magic of that first bite.
sentences.zh: 试图找回第一口的那种神奇感觉。

sentences.en: But it's no use.
sentences.zh: 但无济于事。

sentences.en: What had been unbelievably delicious minutes earlier is now merely pleasant.
sentences.zh: 几分钟前还美味得不可思议的东西，现在变得平平无奇。

sentences.en: What explains this?
sentences.zh: 这该如何解释？

sentences.en: More importantly, what can we do to make the second half of that slice of cake
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，我们能做些什么，让剩下的一半蛋糕

sentences.en: taste as good as the first?
sentences.zh: 吃起来和第一口一样美味呢？

sentences.en: These are questions that animate cognitive neuroscientist Tali Sharratt
sentences.zh: 这些问题正是伦敦大学学院的认知神经科学家塔莉·沙拉特所研究的课题。

sentences.en: at University College London.
sentences.zh: 塔莉·沙拉特，欢迎回到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Tali Sharratt, welcome back to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能回来。

sentences.en: It's a pleasure to be back.
sentences.zh: 塔莉，你曾在多米尼加共和国的一个度假村做过一些研究。

sentences.en: Tali, you did some research in a resort in the Dominican Republic.
sentences.zh: 你能为我描述一下那里的环境，以及你向在那里度假的人提出了什么问题吗？

sentences.en: Can you describe the setting for me and what questions you asked the people who were vacationing there?
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 当时我正在与一家大型旅游公司合作。

sentences.en: So I was working with a big tourism company.
sentences.zh: 他们想知道的是，是什么让人们在度假时感到快乐，

sentences.en: And what they wanted to know is what makes people happy on vacation
sentences.zh: 以及他们在度假的什么时候最快乐？

sentences.en: and when are they the happiest on vacation?
sentences.zh: 所以我们进行了调查，还亲自去了度假村与人们交谈。

sentences.en: So we did surveys and we actually went out to the resorts and we talked to people.
sentences.zh: 当数据汇总后，我们发现了两个非常有趣的现象。

sentences.en: And when the data came in, we found two really interesting things.
sentences.zh: 第一，度假者在度假第43小时时最快乐。

sentences.en: The first was that the holiday makers were the happiest 43 hours in.
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？

sentences.en: Why is that?
sentences.zh: 嗯，43小时让他们有时间安顿下来并整理好行李。

sentences.en: Well, 43 hours allowed them time to get settled and unpack.
sentences.zh: 这样他们就能真正专注于享受乐趣了。

sentences.en: So they could really concentrate on fun.
sentences.zh: 但在此之后，幸福感就开始下降了，对吧？

sentences.en: But after that, happiness starts going down, right?
sentences.zh: 快乐越来越少。

sentences.en: Less and less joy.
sentences.zh: 当然，需要说明的是，他们一直都很开心。

sentences.en: Now, to be clear, they were always happy.
sentences.zh: 但在第八天，他们不像第七天那么开心。

sentences.en: But on day eight, they weren't as happy as they were in day seven.
sentences.zh: 第七天不如第六天，以此类推。

sentences.en: Day seven, not as happy as day six and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 我们发现的第二点是，当我们问他们，

sentences.en: And the second thing that we found is that when we asked them,
sentences.zh: 假期里最棒的部分是什么时，

sentences.en: what was the best part of the holiday?
sentences.zh: 有一个词他们使用的频率最高。

sentences.en: There was one word that they used more than any other word.
sentences.zh: 那个词就是“第一次”。

sentences.en: And that word was firSt.
sentences.zh: 第一次看海，第一杯鸡尾酒，第一个沙堡，

sentences.en: The first view of the ocean, the first cocktail, the first sandcastle,
sentences.zh: 第一次跳进泳池。

sentences.en: the first dip in the pool.
sentences.zh: “第一次”总是令人兴奋且新鲜的。

sentences.en: Firsts were exciting and new.
sentences.zh: 第二次跳进泳池也很好，但不如第一次那么好。

sentences.en: The second dip in the pool was also good, but it wasn't as good as the firSt.
sentences.zh: 我认为这确实是习惯化的一个绝佳例子，对吧？

sentences.en: And this is really, I think, a great example of habituation, right?
sentences.zh: 当你第一次看到大海时，它是美妙的。

sentences.en: When you see the ocean, it's wonderful.
sentences.zh: 第二次看到它时，它依然美妙，

sentences.en: And the second time you see it, it's still wonderful,
sentences.zh: 但不如第一次那么美妙了。

sentences.en: but it's not quite as wonderful as the first time.
sentences.zh: 对于我们周围一直存在、恒定或频繁出现的事物，

sentences.en: Things that are around us all the time, that are constant or that are frequent,
sentences.zh: 我们的情绪反应会减弱。

sentences.en: we just respond less emotionally.
sentences.zh: 甚至在感知上，我们的反应也会变迟钝。

sentences.en: And even perceptually, we respond to them less.
sentences.zh: 心理学家发现同样的现象，

sentences.en: So psychologists have found the same phenomenon happening,
sentences.zh: 不仅发生在吃甜点或度假的人身上，

sentences.en: not just among people eating dessert or going on vacation,
sentences.zh: 也发生在人生中最重要的事件上，比如结婚。

sentences.en: but in relation to the most significant events of life, like getting married.
sentences.zh: 研究显示新婚夫妇的幸福感水平如何？

sentences.en: What does the research show about happiness levels among newlyweds?
sentences.zh: 平均而言，人们结婚时幸福感确实会上升。

sentences.en: Happiness actually goes up when people get married, on average.
sentences.zh: 但随后它会不断下降，

sentences.en: But then it starts going down and down and down,
sentences.zh: 大约两年后，它会回到基准水平，也就是婚前的水平。

sentences.en: and it reaches baseline level, that is the level that before they got married,
sentences.zh: 而且，对伴侣的吸引力也会随着时间的推移而下降。

sentences.en: in about two years.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是为什么许多好莱坞电影以婚礼甚至初吻作为结局。

sentences.en: And also, attraction to their partner goes down over the years.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: I mean, this is why so many Hollywood movies end with the wedding or even the first kiss.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，当我们习惯化时，意味着我们对事物（比如看海）的反应变弱了，

sentences.en: Yes, yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 我们对新恋人的反应也会变弱，对吧？

sentences.en: But, you know, as we habituate, meaning we respond less to things like to the view of the ocean,
sentences.zh: 我们周围恒常存在的事物确实不再那么吸引我们的注意力了，对吧？

sentences.en: we also respond less to our new love, right?
sentences.zh: 我们不太关注它，所以也不会像开始时那样专注于它，

sentences.en: What is around us constantly just doesn't really gather our attention as much, right?
sentences.zh: 它也无法再激起当初那种快乐和兴奋感了。

sentences.en: And we kind of, we don't attend to it, and so we don't really focus in on it as much,
sentences.zh: 所以，在回顾这项研究时，我能想到自己生活中各种各样的事情，

sentences.en: and it doesn't really spark that kind of joy and excitement than it did at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 我感觉自己已经对它们产生了习惯化。

sentences.en: So, as I was reviewing this work, I could think of all kinds of things in my own life
sentences.zh: 塔莉，你肯定也一样。

sentences.en: where I feel I have habituated to things.
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我一些你已经习惯了的事情吗？

sentences.en: The same must be true for you, Tali.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: Can you tell me about some things that you have habituated to?
sentences.zh: 我想可能几乎所有事情都是这样。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 你知道，甚至包括我的工作，对吧？

sentences.en: Probably to almost everything, I would say.
sentences.zh: 如果你回想一下刚得到第一份入门级工作的时候，

sentences.en: You know, even my work, right?
sentences.zh: 那真的很令人兴奋和新鲜，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, if you think about when you first got your first job entry-level position,
sentences.zh: 但过了一段时间，你就习惯了。

sentences.en: it is really exciting and new, right?
sentences.zh: 即使这份工作是你的梦想工作，而且非常有意义，

sentences.en: But after a while, you kind of get used to it.
sentences.zh: 多年以后，它看起来似乎也没那么有趣了。

sentences.en: And even if the job is your dream job, and it's really meaningful work,
sentences.zh: 看起来没那么令人兴奋了。

sentences.en: over the years, it doesn't seem that interesting.
sentences.zh: 塔莉在买下她现在住的房子后，对此有深刻的体会。

sentences.en: It doesn't seem that exciting.
sentences.zh: 我们在疫情期间搬进了这所房子。

sentences.en: Tali experienced this acutely after buying the house she lives in.
sentences.zh: 我们有两个孩子，之前住在城里，

sentences.en: We moved into this house in the middle of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 住在一个对四口之家来说有点太小的地方。

sentences.en: So, we have two kids, and we were living in the city,
sentences.zh: 但在疫情前这没问题，因为我们并不总是待在家里。

sentences.en: in a place that was a little bit too small, I think, for a family of four.
sentences.zh: 但当然，疫情开始了，我们所有人不得不一直待在家里。

sentences.en: But it was fine before the pandemic, because we weren't in the home at all times.
sentences.zh: 孩子们在家学习，所以我们搬到了城外一个更宽敞的地方。

sentences.en: But, of course, then the pandemic started, and so all of us are at home at all times.
sentences.zh: 刚搬进来时，我觉得这里简直是完美的地方，

sentences.en: The kids are studying at home, and so we moved to a much more spacious place outside of the city.
sentences.zh: 它确实给我带来了很多快乐。

sentences.en: And when I first moved, it felt just the perfect place to be,
sentences.zh: 每个人都有自己的房间，还有一个花园，

sentences.en: and it really brought me a lot of joy.
sentences.zh: 到处都是树木和绿植。

sentences.en: Everyone had a room for themselves, and also had a garden,
sentences.zh: 所以，当你从大窗户向外看，看到满眼绿色时，会感到很幸福。

sentences.en: and there was trees and greenery.
sentences.zh: 现在依然如此，但当然，我已经习惯了。

sentences.en: So, you look out of the big windows, and you see all this green, which makes you feel happy.
sentences.zh: 所以，那种反应越来越弱了。

sentences.en: And it still does, but, of course, I got used to it.
sentences.zh: 我们之前在《隐藏的大脑》中讨论过这种现象。

sentences.en: And so, the reaction is less and less and less.
sentences.zh: 心理学家有时称之为“享乐适应”。

sentences.en: So, we've talked about this phenomenon on hidden brain before.
sentences.zh: 对于不熟悉这个术语的听众，你能解释一下它是什么吗？

sentences.en: Psychologists sometimes call this the hedonic treadmill.
sentences.zh: 以及它与你一直在谈论的这种更广泛的现象——习惯化——之间有什么联系？

sentences.en: For listeners who are unfamiliar with the term, can you explain what that is,
sentences.zh: 好的，享乐适应是指人们有一种幸福基准线的观点。

sentences.en: and also the links to this larger phenomenon you've been talking about called habituation?
sentences.zh: 有些人可能比其他人稍微快乐一点。

sentences.en: Yeah, so the hedonic treadmill is this idea that people have a baseline of happiness.
sentences.zh: 我们可以去做一些让我们快乐的事情，比如结婚、找份好工作。

sentences.en: And, you know, some people could be a little bit happier than others.
sentences.zh: 但最终，我们会慢慢地回到这个基准线。

sentences.en: We can go, you know, do something that makes us happy, get married, get a nice job.
sentences.zh: 同样，坏事也会发生在我们身上。

sentences.en: But eventually, we will kind of slowly, slowly go back to this baseline.
sentences.zh: 可能是非常糟糕的事情，比如失去亲人、丢掉工作，

sentences.en: Also, bad things happen to us.
sentences.zh: 当这些事情发生时，我们当然会感觉非常糟糕。

sentences.en: It could be really bad things, lose a loved one, lose your job,
sentences.zh: 但最终，我们会慢慢地回到我们的基准线。

sentences.en: and we would, of course, feel much worse when these things happen.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是享乐适应的基本含义。

sentences.en: But then, eventually, slowly, slowly, slowly, we go back to our baseline.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们正在讨论的现象——习惯化——是相关的，对吧？

sentences.en: So, that's basically the hedonic treadmill.
sentences.zh: 但它并不完全相同。

sentences.en: But I think the phenomena that we're talking about, habituation, is related, right?
sentences.zh: 它的范围要广泛得多。

sentences.en: But it's not quite the same.
sentences.zh: 习惯化意味着我们只是对周围的任何事物做出反应，

sentences.en: It is much, much broader.
sentences.zh: 无论是视觉还是嗅觉。

sentences.en: Habituation means that we just respond to anything that is around us,
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号缺失，根据上下文补全）

sentences.en: anything visual or smell.
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号缺失，根据上下文补全）

sentences.en: So, for example, you go into a room, and you really smell, let's say, roses, right?
sentences.zh: 比如，你走进一个房间，闻到了玫瑰花的香味，对吧？

sentences.en: Within about 20 minutes, you won't be able to perceive the smell of roses,
sentences.zh: 大约20分钟后，你就闻不到玫瑰花的味道了，

sentences.en: because your olfactory neurons will just not respond anymore.
sentences.zh: 因为你的嗅觉神经元不再做出反应了。

sentences.en: Or you hear the noise of the AC in the background, and it could be quite irritating at first, but very quickly, you just don't notice it anymore, right?
sentences.zh: 或者你听到了背景中空调的噪音，起初可能觉得很烦人，但很快，你就完全注意不到了，对吧？

sentences.en: So, these are perceptual examples, but our emotional reactions to things, it could be a dog barking, it's like the neighbor got a new dog, and it's really scary.
sentences.zh: 这些是感知方面的例子，但我们对事物的各种情绪反应也是如此，比如邻居养了条新狗，一直在叫，这真的很吓人。

sentences.en: And we have a fear reaction, but the second time, less so, and the third time, less so.
sentences.zh: 我们会有恐惧反应，但第二次反应就没那么强烈了，第三次就更弱了。

sentences.en: So, there's perceptual habituation, there's emotional habituation, and it has a lot of implications beyond the hedonic treadmill to our personal life, but also to society.
sentences.zh: 所以，存在感知习惯化，也存在情绪习惯化，这不仅对我们的个人生活，甚至对整个社会，除了“享乐适应”之外，还有很多深远的影响。

sentences.en: So, why does this happen, Tali?
sentences.zh: 那么，塔莉，这是为什么呢？

sentences.en: Why is it that the brain habituates to things?
sentences.zh: 为什么大脑会对事物产生习惯化？

sentences.en: At a fundamental level, it seems like it's a property of the brain.
sentences.zh: 从根本上讲，这似乎是大脑的一种特性。

sentences.en: Why does this happen?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, there is an evolutionary advantage, right?
sentences.zh: 这其实是有进化优势的，对吧？

sentences.en: The brain has limited resources, and so, once we've processed something, then it's really time for the brain to keep the resources for the next thing that is coming our way.
sentences.zh: 大脑的资源是有限的，所以一旦我们处理完某件事，大脑就真的需要把资源留给接下来要处理的事情。

sentences.en: So, imagine there's a dog, and the dog is in the rose garden, and, you know, the smell of roses really fills its nostrils.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，有一只狗在玫瑰园里，你知道，玫瑰的香味充斥着它的鼻腔。

sentences.en: It is helpful that after a while, the olfactory neurons will just stop responding,
sentences.zh: 过了一会儿，嗅觉神经元停止反应是有好处的，

sentences.en: so now we have all the resources needed for the dog to be able to smell a coyote that is coming its way.
sentences.zh: 这样我们就有足够的资源让狗去嗅出正在靠近的郊狼。

sentences.en: So, we need to be prepared for these threats that are coming our way, so we need the resources, but also for the good things.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们需要为即将到来的威胁做好准备，因此需要资源，对于好事也是如此。

sentences.en: Maybe there's a cookie somewhere in the distance that the dog should go and get.
sentences.zh: 也许远处有一块饼干，狗应该去把它找出来。

sentences.en: So, that has an evolutionary advantage, but it also keeps us motivated.
sentences.zh: 所以，这具有进化优势，同时也让我们保持动力。

sentences.en: So, if you think back to your entry-level job, and you were super happy about it, imagine you stayed super happy forever.
sentences.zh: 回想一下你刚入职时的那份工作，你当时非常开心，想象一下如果你永远保持那种极度快乐的状态。

sentences.en: You will not be motivated to get to the next promotion, right, to get to the next job.
sentences.zh: 你就不会有动力去争取下一次晋升，或者去寻找下一份工作了，对吧？

sentences.en: You'll just stay where you are.
sentences.zh: 你只会停滞不前。

sentences.en: So, we need habituation in order to evolve as a person, but also as a society.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们需要习惯化才能作为个人乃至社会不断进化。

sentences.en: And maybe the third important factor is well-being and mental health.
sentences.zh: 也许第三个重要因素是幸福感和心理健康。

sentences.en: So, what has been shown is that people with mental health problems, for example, depression, tend to habituate slower.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，有心理健康问题的人，例如抑郁症患者，习惯化的速度往往较慢。

sentences.en: People with depression, when negative things happen, they don't bounce back as faSt.
sentences.zh: 抑郁症患者在遇到负面事件时，恢复得没那么快。

sentences.en: There's a great study that was conducted by Professor Aaron Heller from the University of Miami,
sentences.zh: 迈阿密大学的亚伦·海勒教授做过一项很棒的研究，

sentences.en: where he asked students who just got a score on a really important test how they were feeling.
sentences.zh: 他询问刚拿到重要考试成绩的学生感觉如何。

sentences.en: And then 45 minutes later, he asked them how they were feeling.
sentences.zh: 45分钟后，他又问了他们同样的问题。

sentences.en: And 45 minutes later, how they were feeling.
sentences.zh: 再过45分钟，又问了一次。

sentences.en: And did that for the rest of the day and the next day.
sentences.zh: 他在当天余下的时间和第二天都重复了这一过程。

sentences.en: And what he found is that those without a history of depression and those with a history of depression, they all felt really bad at the beginning, if they got a bad grade.
sentences.zh: 他发现，无论是否有抑郁症病史，如果成绩不好，大家一开始都会感觉很糟糕。

sentences.en: But the difference was that those that did not have a history of depression, they, after a few hours, they were back at baseline, right?
sentences.zh: 但区别在于，没有抑郁症病史的人，几个小时后就恢复到基准水平了，对吧？

sentences.en: They were doing their things, going out.
sentences.zh: 他们继续做自己的事，出去玩。

sentences.en: But those with a history of depression or current depression, they tend to ruminate.
sentences.zh: 但那些有抑郁症病史或正处于抑郁状态的人，往往会陷入反刍思维。

sentences.en: They weren't able to go back to just their level of well-being that they were before, right?
sentences.zh: 他们无法回到之前的幸福水平，对吧？

sentences.en: They were kind of stuck and habituated much, much slower.
sentences.zh: 他们被困住了，习惯化的速度要慢得多。

sentences.en: You say that in order to survive and reproduce, we need to prioritize what is new and different.
sentences.zh: 你说过，为了生存和繁衍，我们需要优先关注那些新鲜和不同的事物。

sentences.en: So the sudden smell of smoke or a rustle in the bushes that could signal a lion or a predator, you know, an attractive potential mate who passes by.
sentences.zh: 比如突然闻到的烟味，或者灌木丛中的沙沙声，那可能预示着狮子或捕食者的出现，又或者是一个路过的迷人异性。

sentences.en: You say to make the new and the unexpected stand out, your brain filters out the old and expected.
sentences.zh: 你说为了让新鲜和意想不到的事物脱颖而出，大脑会过滤掉陈旧和预期之中的事物。

sentences.en: So in some ways, this is really a fundamental property of the brain that's really been designed through millions of years of evolution.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种程度上说，这确实是大脑的一种基本特性，是经过数百万年进化设计出来的。

sentences.en: Yes, and habituation is something that we could see in all animals, whether it is a rodent or a dog or a fish.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们在所有动物身上都能看到习惯化，无论是啮齿动物、狗还是鱼。

sentences.en: And in fact, we can see something very similar, what we call neural adaptation, in even bacteria.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们甚至在细菌身上也能看到非常类似的情况，我们称之为神经适应。

sentences.en: So this is something that goes way, way, way back and is really fundamental.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种非常古老且根本的机制。

sentences.en: I mean, every neuron in our brain habituates.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们大脑中的每一个神经元都会习惯化。

sentences.en: Our brains painstakingly construct models of what the world is like.
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑费尽心思地构建着关于世界样貌的模型。

sentences.en: When reality conforms to that model, we don't react or even notice it very much.
sentences.zh: 当现实符合那个模型时，我们就不会做出反应，甚至根本不会注意到它。

sentences.en: When we come back, how to step off the hedonic treadmill and feel the goodness of good things again.
sentences.zh: 回来后，我们将探讨如何摆脱“享乐适应”，重新感受美好事物的快乐。

sentences.en: Also, we'll explore the flip side of the hedonic treadmill, the way we habituate to things that are scary, shady and sad.
sentences.zh: 此外，我们还将探讨“享乐适应”的另一面，即我们如何对那些可怕、阴暗和悲伤的事物产生习惯化。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 你正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Tali Sharath is a cognitive neuroscientist at University College London.
sentences.zh: 塔莉·沙罗特是伦敦大学学院的认知神经科学家。

sentences.en: With Cass Sunstein, she's the author of Look Again, The Power of Noticing What Was Always There.
sentences.zh: 她与卡斯·桑斯坦合著了《再看一眼：注意到一直存在的事物的力量》一书。

sentences.en: Tali, you've told us how the process of habituation can diminish the pleasure and satisfaction that an event or an experience might once have given us.
sentences.zh: 塔莉，你告诉过我们，习惯化过程是如何削弱一个事件或经历曾经带给我们的快乐和满足感的。

sentences.en: You say that there's a solution to this that you call dishabituation.
sentences.zh: 你说对此有一个解决方案，你称之为“去习惯化”。

sentences.en: What do you mean by the term?
sentences.zh: 你所说的这个词是什么意思？

sentences.en: So, dishabituation means starting to respond again to something that we stopped responding because it was around us all the time.
sentences.zh: “去习惯化”是指重新开始对那些因为一直存在而不再做出反应的事物产生反应。

sentences.en: So, we start noticing it, feeling it, perceptually reacting to it.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，我们开始注意到它、感受它，并在感知上做出反应。

sentences.en: And if it's something good, the joy comes back.
sentences.zh: 如果那是件好事，快乐就会回归。

sentences.en: If it's something bad, we feel the negative feelings again.
sentences.zh: 如果那是件坏事，我们就会再次感受到负面情绪。

sentences.en: So, you once got a clue on how dishabituation might work from a story told by the movie star Julia Roberts.
sentences.zh: 你曾经从电影明星朱莉娅·罗伯茨讲述的一个故事中，得到了关于“去习惯化”如何运作的启发。

sentences.en: Tell me that story.
sentences.zh: 讲讲那个故事吧。

sentences.en: She was describing her daily life, how she wakes up in the morning and she makes breakfast for the kids.
sentences.zh: 她描述了自己的日常生活，每天早上醒来给孩子们做早餐。

sentences.en: She drops them off at school.
sentences.zh: 送他们去学校。

sentences.en: She comes back home.
sentences.zh: 然后回到家。

sentences.en: She maybe has lunch with her husband.
sentences.zh: 也许会和丈夫一起吃午饭。

sentences.en: She does some chores and then she picks them up from the school, makes dinner.
sentences.zh: 做些家务，然后去学校接他们，准备晚餐。

sentences.en: And she says, if I was here for the last 18 years doing that all day, every day, it probably wouldn't still have pixie dust on it.
sentences.zh: 她说，如果我过去18年每天都在重复这些，它可能就不会再有那种神奇的魔力了。

sentences.en: But I go away and I miss it so much and I come back and it kind of resparkles.
sentences.zh: 但我离开一段时间，就会非常想念它，等我回来时，它似乎又重新焕发了光彩。

sentences.en: I mean, that quote is great, but the word resparkles is something that we really liked, right?
sentences.zh: 那段话很棒，但“重新焕发光彩”这个词我们真的很喜欢，对吧？

sentences.en: How do you just take the ordinary life and make it resparkle?
sentences.zh: 你如何让平凡的生活重新焕发光彩？

sentences.en: And what Julia is saying is, well, every time she goes away and then she comes back, then she dishabituates, right?
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅的意思是，每次她离开再回来，她就经历了“去习惯化”，对吧？

sentences.en: Because habituation is something that happens when things are always there, something constant, something frequent.
sentences.zh: 因为习惯化发生在事物一直存在、恒定且频繁的时候。

sentences.en: But if you are not in that situation, if you go away, then when you come back, then you feel it again.
sentences.zh: 但如果你不在那种环境中，如果你离开，当你回来时，你就会重新感受到它。

sentences.en: And if it's good, then it will resparkle.
sentences.zh: 如果它是好的，它就会重新焕发光彩。

sentences.en: So in some ways, the going away is an essential component of the coming back with joy.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种程度上说，离开是带着喜悦回归的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: Yeah, indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And in fact, after we wrote the book and, you know, I actually heard this podcast with Jodie Foster.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在我们写完书之后，我听了朱迪·福斯特的播客。

sentences.en: And she talks about how she was away on set filming for six months and then she got back home.
sentences.zh: 她谈到自己在片场拍了六个月的戏，然后回到了家。

sentences.en: And this is what she said.
sentences.zh: 她是这样说的。

sentences.en: She said, I came back from somewhere that is amazing and beautiful, but you know, you long for really dumb things that you're just used to.
sentences.zh: 她说，我从一个令人惊叹且美丽的地方回来，但你知道，你会渴望那些你已经习以为常的琐事。

sentences.en: That six months ago, I'm sure I was bored by it.
sentences.zh: 六个月前，我肯定对这些感到厌烦。

sentences.en: But right now I'm like, my God, avocados are amazing.
sentences.zh: 但现在我觉得，天哪，牛油果太棒了。

sentences.en: Or I'm so glad I get to go to the gym again.
sentences.zh: 或者我很高兴又能去健身房了。

sentences.en: Things that six months ago were sort of what I was trying to escape from.
sentences.zh: 这些六个月前我试图逃避的事情，

sentences.en: Now everything is amazing.
sentences.zh: 现在一切都变得太棒了。

sentences.en: I mean, I can tell you that when I go away for a long time and I come back, I just have this joy.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我可以告诉你，当我离开很长一段时间再回来时，我真的会感到喜悦。

sentences.en: You know, my bed is like amazing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的床简直太棒了。

sentences.en: And then, you know, the view from the window is amazing.
sentences.zh: 还有窗外的景色，也太棒了。

sentences.en: Now you might not be a Hollywood star who goes away for months on end to shoot movies in glamorous locations.
sentences.zh: 你可能不是那种为了在迷人的地方拍电影而一走就是几个月的好莱坞明星。

sentences.en: That's okay.
sentences.zh: 没关系。

sentences.en: You can get the ordinary things in your life to re-sparkle just by getting up and going for a walk.
sentences.zh: 你只需要起身去散散步，就能让生活中的平凡事物重新焕发光彩。

sentences.en: Or even wandering into the next room.
sentences.zh: 甚至只是溜达到隔壁房间。

sentences.en: So, I mean, there's all levels of habituation, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，习惯化是有各个层级的，对吧？

sentences.en: If I'm now sitting in one room, I'm going to move to the kitchen.
sentences.zh: 如果我现在坐在这个房间里，我要搬到厨房去。

sentences.en: What I see, what I smell is all going to be different.
sentences.zh: 我看到的、闻到的都会有所不同。

sentences.en: It means I'm going to have different information coming into my brain.
sentences.zh: 这意味着会有不同的信息进入我的大脑。

sentences.en: But also, my brain will be all set up for change.
sentences.zh: 而且，我的大脑也会为变化做好准备。

sentences.en: So, it's been shown that if you change your environment, even these small changes.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，如果你改变环境，哪怕是这些微小的改变。

sentences.en: You sit in the office and then you get up and you just go for a walk or you work in a coffee shop.
sentences.zh: 你坐在办公室里，然后起身去散步，或者在咖啡馆工作。

sentences.en: Any one of those changes enhances your creativity.
sentences.zh: 任何这些改变都能增强你的创造力。

sentences.en: Now, granted, the studies show that the effect lasts for about six minutes.
sentences.zh: 当然，研究显示这种效果大约持续六分钟。

sentences.en: Every time you change, it lasts only for about six minutes on average, which is small.
sentences.zh: 每次你改变环境，平均只能持续六分钟，这很短。

sentences.en: But, however, many times that's all the amount that you need to find that solution that you were thinking of.
sentences.zh: 但是，很多时候，这正是你找到那个苦思冥想的解决方案所需要的时长。

sentences.en: Or that new idea that is going to change, you know, what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 或者那个即将改变你所做之事的全新想法。

sentences.en: I mean, I definitely have examples of that happening.
sentences.zh: 我确实有这样的亲身经历。

sentences.en: If I think I can really remember every time that I had an idea that would change the course of my research and would be very important for what I do for many years to come.
sentences.zh: 我真的记得每一次我产生了一个能改变我研究方向、并对我未来多年的工作产生重要影响的想法时，

sentences.en: And in every single incident, I was not in front of my computer working, right?
sentences.zh: 在每一个案例中，我当时都没有坐在电脑前工作，对吧？

sentences.en: So, one example is I was in my office.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，当时我在办公室。

sentences.en: I was trying to solve this problem.
sentences.zh: 我正试图解决一个问题。

sentences.en: We had this data and we couldn't make sense of it.
sentences.zh: 我们有这些数据，但无法解读。

sentences.en: Why is it happening?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？

sentences.en: Couldn't solve it.
sentences.zh: 怎么也解决不了。

sentences.en: And I said, okay, I'm going to go to the gym.
sentences.zh: 于是我说，好吧，我要去健身房。

sentences.en: Left the office, started walking towards the gym.
sentences.zh: 离开了办公室，开始往健身房走。

sentences.en: I didn't even get to the gym.
sentences.zh: 我甚至还没到健身房。

sentences.en: And the solution just came to me.
sentences.zh: 解决方案就突然出现在我脑海里了。

sentences.en: Another example is I was, again, in my office working.
sentences.zh: 另一个例子是，当时我还在办公室工作。

sentences.en: But then I decided to have a little break.
sentences.zh: 但我决定休息一下。

sentences.en: And I opened up the New York Times science section.
sentences.zh: 我打开了《纽约时报》的科学版块。

sentences.en: And I read about a study in Monkees about how monkeys really enjoy getting information.
sentences.zh: 我读到了一项关于猴子的研究，发现猴子非常喜欢获取信息。

sentences.en: Even if the information they can't use for any reason altogether, they really like it.
sentences.zh: 即使这些信息它们根本无法使用，它们也非常喜欢。

sentences.en: And the dopamine neurons, dopamine is important for our reward system, they are activated when the monkey gets information.
sentences.zh: 多巴胺神经元——多巴胺对我们的奖励系统很重要——在猴子获得信息时会被激活。

sentences.en: And the monkeys like it so much, they're even willing to give up some of their water in order to get more information.
sentences.zh: 猴子非常喜欢，甚至愿意放弃一些水来获取更多信息。

sentences.en: And so I thought that was really interesting.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这非常有趣。

sentences.en: And that will eventually trigger research that I did on humans on the value of information.
sentences.zh: 这最终促成了我后来对人类信息价值的研究。

sentences.en: We know that some pleasures lose their sparkle very quickly.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，有些快乐会很快失去光彩。

sentences.en: We've all been excited about some new purchase, only to see it gather dust in a corner before too long.
sentences.zh: 我们都曾为某次新购物而兴奋，结果没过多久，它就在角落里落满了灰尘。

sentences.en: But you say there are some experiences that retain the capacity to generate happiness over time.
sentences.zh: 但你说有些经历能长期保持产生快乐的能力。

sentences.en: Explain the difference and what do you think is going on?
sentences.zh: 解释一下区别，你认为发生了什么？

sentences.en: So material goods, you can buy something and you can use it for years, right?
sentences.zh: 物质商品，你可以买一件东西并使用多年，对吧？

sentences.en: Maybe it's a piece of clothing, maybe it's a TV, but probably the joy that you get will just go down over time.
sentences.zh: 也许是一件衣服，也许是一台电视，但你从中获得的快乐可能会随着时间的推移而减少。

sentences.en: Now here's the interesting thing.
sentences.zh: 有趣的地方在于：

sentences.en: When it comes to experiences, maybe you went on vacation to Thailand, maybe you went to a concert, right?
sentences.zh: 当谈到经历时，也许你去泰国度假了，也许你去听了一场音乐会，对吧？

sentences.en: You saw Amy Winehouse before she died.
sentences.zh: 你在艾米·怀恩豪斯去世前看过她的演出。

sentences.en: And the reason that they tend to habituate slower is because they stay in your mind, right?
sentences.zh: 它们习惯化较慢的原因是它们留在了你的脑海里，对吧？

sentences.en: So they come up in your mind when you recollect them rather than kind of processing them in front of us.
sentences.zh: 当你回忆它们时，它们会浮现在脑海中，而不是像物质商品那样在我们面前被处理。

sentences.en: And so this was actually shown in a study that the rate of habituation for material goods is faster than the rate of habituation for experiences.
sentences.zh: 这在研究中得到了证实：物质商品的习惯化速度比经历的习惯化速度要快。

sentences.en: So we're also slower to habituate to the pleasures of giving compared to the pleasures of receiving.
sentences.zh: 所以，与接受带来的快乐相比，我们对给予带来的快乐习惯化得也更慢。

sentences.en: Can you talk about this idea, Tali?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这个观点吗，塔莉？

sentences.en: Yeah, so there was a study that was conducted where in one condition, they gave people $5 and they said,
sentences.zh: 好的，曾有一项研究，在一种情况下，他们给人们5美元，并说：

sentences.en: take the $5 and buy whatever you want for yourself.
sentences.zh: 拿着这5美元，给自己买任何你想要的东西。

sentences.en: You know, you could buy a coffee, you could buy a pen.
sentences.zh: 你可以买杯咖啡，或者买支笔。

sentences.en: Day number two, $5.
sentences.zh: 第二天，又是5美元。

sentences.en: Buy whatever you like.
sentences.zh: 买任何你喜欢的。

sentences.en: Day number three, $5.
sentences.zh: 第三天，又是5美元。

sentences.en: And they did that for a few days.
sentences.zh: 他们连续几天都这样做。

sentences.en: And every time they asked the people, well, how much did you enjoy whatever you got with those $5?
sentences.zh: 每次他们问人们，你从那5美元里得到了多少快乐？

sentences.en: In another condition, they gave people again $5.
sentences.zh: 在另一种情况下，他们又给了人们5美元。

sentences.en: But this time they said, buy something for someone else.
sentences.zh: 但这次他们说，去给别人买点东西。

sentences.en: So this time you're buying coffee for your colleague or you're buying a pen for your child, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这次你是给同事买咖啡，或者给孩子买支笔，对吧？

sentences.en: And every day they give them $5 and they would buy something for someone else.
sentences.zh: 每天他们都给这笔钱，让他们去给别人买东西。

sentences.en: And they asked them, how much did you enjoy this?
sentences.zh: 然后问他们，你从中得到了多少快乐？

sentences.en: How much, you know, how good did it make you feel?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这让你感觉有多好？

sentences.en: Now, what's interesting in this study is they looked at the rates of habituation, right?
sentences.zh: 这项研究有趣的地方在于，他们观察了习惯化的比率，对吧？

sentences.en: In both cases, the $5 will give you less joy over the days.
sentences.zh: 在这两种情况下，这5美元带来的快乐都会随着时间的推移而减少。

sentences.en: But the rate of habituation was much faster when you got things for yourself than when you got it for someone else.
sentences.zh: 但当你为自己买东西时，习惯化的速度要比为别人买东西时快得多。

sentences.en: And I think perhaps the reason is that the joy that you get from giving is not just pure happiness, it is meaning as well.
sentences.zh: 我想原因可能在于，给予带来的快乐不仅仅是纯粹的幸福，它还包含意义。

sentences.en: There's a meaningful act in giving to someone else.
sentences.zh: 为他人付出是一种有意义的行为。

sentences.en: And while the feeling of meaning can also habituate, it probably habituates slower than just pure joy of, you know, drinking the coffee or using your sparkly pen.
sentences.zh: 虽然意义感也会产生习惯化，但它可能比喝咖啡或使用闪亮钢笔带来的纯粹快乐习惯化得更慢。

sentences.en: You say that another way we can thwart habituation is by seeking out opportunities to learn.
sentences.zh: 你说我们可以通过寻求学习机会来抵御习惯化。

sentences.en: Talk about this idea.
sentences.zh: 谈谈这个想法。

sentences.en: How is curiosity and learning, how can they be engines or defenses against habituation?
sentences.zh: 好奇心和学习是如何成为抵御习惯化的引擎或防御手段的？

sentences.en: So when you ask people, what is a good life?
sentences.zh: 当你问人们什么是美好的生活时，

sentences.en: What do you see as a good life?
sentences.zh: 你认为什么是美好的生活？

sentences.en: Usually people will say, I want to feel joy, right?
sentences.zh: 人们通常会说，我想感受快乐，对吧？

sentences.en: I don't want to feel sad.
sentences.zh: 我不想感到悲伤。

sentences.en: And they usually say, what do I want meaning in my life?
sentences.zh: 他们通常还会说，我想要生活中有意义。

sentences.en: And then there's a third thing that tends to be an element of a good life, which people don't usually think about so much, which is variety.
sentences.zh: 还有第三点，它往往是美好生活的一个要素，但人们通常不太会想到，那就是多样性。

sentences.en: It turns out that variety is something that enhances people's psychological experiences, right?
sentences.zh: 事实证明，多样性能够增强人们的心理体验，对吧？

sentences.en: It gives you like a rich psychological experience.
sentences.zh: 它能给你带来丰富的心理体验。

sentences.en: And why is that helpful?
sentences.zh: 为什么这很有帮助呢？

sentences.en: And there's a few answers to this.
sentences.zh: 对此有几个答案。

sentences.en: One is that variety means that we will habituate less to things because it's changing all the time, right?
sentences.zh: 其一是多样性意味着我们对事物的习惯化会减少，因为一切都在不断变化，对吧？

sentences.en: We're doing one thing, we're doing the other thing, right?
sentences.zh: 我们做这件事，又做那件事，对吧？

sentences.en: So variety actually counters the effects of habituation.
sentences.zh: 所以多样性实际上抵消了习惯化的影响。

sentences.en: But the other reason is, if you have variety in your life, you work on different projects, you talk to different types of people, you are in different places,
sentences.zh: 但另一个原因是，如果你的生活丰富多样，你从事不同的项目，与不同类型的人交谈，身处不同的地方，

sentences.en: it always involves learning.
sentences.zh: 这总是涉及学习。

sentences.en: And the thing about learning is, learning means that there is a change.
sentences.zh: 而关于学习的一点是，学习意味着变化。

sentences.en: You cannot habituate to change, by definition.
sentences.zh: 根据定义，你无法对变化产生习惯化。

sentences.en: Gaining knowledge is processed in the brain like food, like water, like sex.
sentences.zh: 获取知识在大脑中的处理方式就像食物、水和性一样。

sentences.en: There is the response that we have when we are learning something new, which, you know, why do people enjoy podcasts so much, right?
sentences.zh: 当我们学习新事物时，我们会产生一种反应，你知道，为什么人们那么喜欢播客，对吧？

sentences.en: Because you're always learning, you're gaining knowledge, and your brain responds to that like it does to chocolate, but you don't get fat.
sentences.zh: 因为你一直在学习，在获取知识，你的大脑对它的反应就像对巧克力一样，但你不会发胖。

sentences.en: So let's go back to the example of eating dessert or going on a vacation.
sentences.zh: 让我们回到吃甜点或去度假的例子。

sentences.en: Many of us assume that when it comes to pleasant or joyful experiences, it's best to enjoy these experiences without interruption.
sentences.zh: 我们许多人认为，当谈到令人愉悦或快乐的体验时，最好不要中断地享受这些体验。

sentences.en: But from what you're saying in the last few minutes, I'm not sure that's true.
sentences.zh: 但根据你过去几分钟所说的，我不确定这是真的。

sentences.en: Is it, Tali?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗，塔莉？

sentences.en: Yeah, no, it's not.
sentences.zh: 是的，不，不是这样的。

sentences.en: Because, let's go back to the vacation example.
sentences.zh: 因为，让我们回到度假的例子。

sentences.en: The most, like, happiest time was 43 hours in.
sentences.zh: 最快乐的时光是在度假开始后的43小时。

sentences.en: And the word that they used most to describe the best parts of the vacation was first, first, first, firSt.
sentences.zh: 他们用来描述度假最美好部分的词汇是：第一次、第一次、第一次、第一次。

sentences.en: So then really what that means is that you want to create more firsts.
sentences.zh: 所以这实际上意味着你想要创造更多的“第一次”。

sentences.en: You want to create more 43 hours in, right?
sentences.zh: 你想要创造更多像那43小时一样的时刻，对吧？

sentences.en: So instead of going for a long two-week vacation somewhere, you might choose to go on shorter, maybe like a long weekend or, you know, maybe just a weekend.
sentences.zh: 所以与其去某个地方进行为期两周的长假，你可能选择去短一点的，比如长周末，或者，你知道，可能只是一个周末。

sentences.en: So take a few short vacations rather than the long one to get more of these exciting novel things.
sentences.zh: 所以多去几次短假，而不是一次长假，这样能获得更多令人兴奋的新鲜事物。

sentences.en: And there's empirical evidence to support this.
sentences.zh: 而且有实证证据支持这一点。

sentences.en: So there is a great study where people were asked, think about a song that you really like.
sentences.zh: 有一个很棒的研究，人们被问到：想一首你非常喜欢的歌。

sentences.en: And what do you think?
sentences.zh: 你觉得呢？

sentences.en: Would you enjoy it more if you listened to the song from beginning to end with no interruptions?
sentences.zh: 如果你从头到尾不间断地听这首歌，你会更享受吗？

sentences.en: Or if you had interruptions, so you listen to the song 20 seconds and a little interruption, 20 seconds and a little interruption.
sentences.zh: 还是说如果中间有中断，比如听20秒停一下，再听20秒再停一下，你会更享受？

sentences.en: 99% of people said, I want to hear the song from beginning to end.
sentences.zh: 99%的人说，我想从头到尾听完这首歌。

sentences.en: I do not want any interruptions, right?
sentences.zh: 我不想要任何中断，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, it seems obvious.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这看起来很明显。

sentences.en: But when they then did the test and they tested how much people enjoyed the song with or without interruptions,
sentences.zh: 但当他们进行测试，考察人们在有或没有中断的情况下对歌曲的享受程度时，

sentences.en: what they find is that people enjoy the song more if it was interrupted.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，如果歌曲被打断，人们反而更享受。

sentences.en: And they were willing to pay twice as much to hear the song in concert, which is super counterintuitive.
sentences.zh: 而且他们愿意花两倍的钱去听现场音乐会，这非常反直觉。

sentences.en: And they did the same.
sentences.zh: 他们做了同样的事。

sentences.en: They did the same study with massages.
sentences.zh: 他们对按摩也做了同样的研究。

sentences.en: Do you want to have the massage from beginning to end, no interruptions?
sentences.zh: 你是想从头到尾不间断地享受按摩吗？

sentences.en: Or do you want to have it with breaks?
sentences.zh: 还是想中间有休息？

sentences.en: People want it beginning to end, no interruptions, but in fact, enjoy it more if there are breaks.
sentences.zh: 人们想要从头到尾不间断，但事实上，如果有间歇，他们会更享受。

sentences.en: And there is an economist named Typer Skitovsky, who has a quote which really puts this in a great sentence,
sentences.zh: 有一位名叫泰伯·斯基托夫斯基的经济学家，他的一句话很好地总结了这一点，

sentences.en: which he says, pleasure results from incomplete and intermittent satisfaction of desires.
sentences.zh: 他说，快乐源于欲望的不完全和间歇性的满足。

sentences.en: So break up the good experiences into bits to enjoy it more.
sentences.zh: 所以把美好的体验拆分成小块，这样能享受得更多。

sentences.en: In other words, when you order the chocolate cake at the restaurant, you know, eat half a slice because that's the slice that's actually going to give you a lot of pleasure.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，当你在餐厅点巧克力蛋糕时，吃半块就够了，因为那半块才是真正能给你带来巨大快乐的部分。

sentences.en: Take the rest home and eat it at home an hour later, and you'll enjoy the second half of the slice as much as the first compared to eating it all together in one go.
sentences.zh: 把剩下的带回家，一小时后再吃，你会发现享受第二半块的快乐程度和第一半块一样，而不是一次性全部吃完。

sentences.en: Or even better, give the second half to your partner.
sentences.zh: 或者更好的是，把剩下的一半给你的伴侣。

sentences.en: So on the flip side, we often do try to break up unpleasant experiences so we don't have to deal with all of it at once.
sentences.zh: 反过来说，我们经常试图拆分不愉快的体验，这样就不必一次性面对所有这些。

sentences.en: So, you know, we say, I need to clean my bathroom, but maybe I'll do part of it on a Saturday and part of it on a Sunday.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们会说，我需要打扫浴室，但也许我周六做一部分，周日做一部分。

sentences.en: Is that a good idea or a terrible idea?
sentences.zh: 这是个好主意还是个糟糕的主意？

sentences.en: For the bad stuff, you want to, we say, swallow the bad hole.
sentences.zh: 对于糟糕的事情，我们说，要“一口气吞下苦果”。

sentences.en: So, for example, if you think about something that you don't like to do, maybe for me, it's like household chores or grading papers.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果你想到某件你不喜欢做的事，对我来说，可能是家务或批改试卷。

sentences.en: If I do maybe like 15 minutes and a break, 20 minutes and a break, what happens is that I'm breaking my habituation to the bad.
sentences.zh: 如果我做15分钟休息一下，再做20分钟休息一下，结果就是我打破了对糟糕事物的习惯化。

sentences.en: So if you're doing like cleaning, for example, there's maybe like a bad smell of the cleaning products, but you habituate to it so you don't smell it anymore.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在打扫卫生，比如，清洁产品可能有难闻的气味，但你习惯了它，所以你闻不到了。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: And that's good.
sentences.zh: 那是好事。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: But if I then break it, I have a little break and I have a cup of coffee and then I go back and I start the chore again, well, then I'm going to feel again bad.
sentences.zh: 但如果我中途休息，喝杯咖啡，然后再回去重新开始做家务，那么，我就会再次感到不适。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: I'm going to like perceive the smell and all of that.
sentences.zh: 我会再次闻到那种气味，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And again, there's empirical data when they actually did the test with people listening to really annoying sounds.
sentences.zh: 同样，当他们对听着令人讨厌的声音的人进行测试时，也有实证数据支持这一点。

sentences.en: And they found, yes, if you just get it over with, you don't rate it as bad, but if you kind of chop it into bits, then you rate the experience as much worse.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，是的，如果你只是尽快做完，你不会觉得它那么糟糕，但如果你把它拆成碎片，你就会觉得这种体验糟糕得多。

sentences.en: It's so interesting that our intuitions in both cases are exactly the opposite of what actually we should be doing.
sentences.zh: 很有趣的是，我们在两种情况下的直觉恰恰与我们实际应该做的相反。

sentences.en: So we have a reluctance to break up pleasant experiences.
sentences.zh: 我们不愿拆分愉快的体验。

sentences.en: We want to take them all in at once.
sentences.zh: 我们想一次性全部吸收。

sentences.en: And we do want to break up unpleasant experiences and not take them in at once.
sentences.zh: 而我们确实想拆分不愉快的体验，不想一次性面对。

sentences.en: And the advice actually in both situations is to do exactly the opposite.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，在这两种情况下的建议都是做完全相反的事。

sentences.en: Yeah, and you know, there's sayings about like savoring or about like, oh, get it over and done with.
sentences.zh: 是的，你知道，有一些关于“细细品味”或者“尽快做完”的说法。

sentences.en: But then in reality, it's really hard, right?
sentences.zh: 但在现实中，这真的很难，对吧？

sentences.en: It's hard to savor.
sentences.zh: 细细品味很难。

sentences.en: We, you know, if there's something good, we don't want to stop.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果有好事，我们不想停下来。

sentences.en: And it's really hard when we're doing something unpleasant not to take breaks.
sentences.zh: 而当我们做不愉快的事情时，不休息真的很难。

sentences.en: So I think the wisdom is there in the culture, but not necessarily something that we do practically.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为文化中存在这种智慧，但未必是我们实际会去做的事情。

sentences.en: Even if the wisdom is difficult to follow, it may seem straightforward.
sentences.zh: 即使这种智慧难以遵循，它看起来也可能很简单。

sentences.en: Power through unpleasant tasks so you don't have to experience the unpleasantness anew by coming back to them multiple times.
sentences.zh: 咬牙完成不愉快的任务，这样你就不用通过多次重复来重新体验那种不快。

sentences.en: With your pleasant experiences, do the opposite.
sentences.zh: 对于愉快的体验，做相反的事。

sentences.en: Break them up so that you can maximize the delight they give you.
sentences.zh: 把它们拆分开来，这样你就能最大化它们带给你的快乐。

sentences.en: Seems simple, right?
sentences.zh: 看起来很简单，对吧？

sentences.en: There's a catch, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，有个陷阱。

sentences.en: Not all unpleasant experiences are created equal.
sentences.zh: 并非所有不愉快的体验都是一样的。

sentences.en: And in some cases, there's a very real cost that comes from numbing ourselves to their unpleasantness.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，让自己对不快变得麻木会带来非常现实的代价。

sentences.en: When we come back, how our minds habituate to things like danger, dishonesty, and discrimination.
sentences.zh: 当我们回来时，我们将探讨我们的思想如何对危险、不诚实和歧视等事物产生习惯化。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 你正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Across every domain of our lives, our minds have a tendency to get accustomed to things.
sentences.zh: 在我们生活的各个领域，我们的思想都有习惯于事物的倾向。

sentences.en: In fact, the brain seems evolutionarily designed to focus on the new and unexpected, on novel threats and opportunities.
sentences.zh: 事实上，大脑似乎在进化上就是为了专注于新的和意想不到的事物，专注于新的威胁和机会。

sentences.en: In our daily lives, this means we take wonderful things for granted.
sentences.zh: 在日常生活中，这意味着我们将美好的事物视为理所当然。

sentences.en: We cease to appreciate amazing people in our lives or the good fortune of being healthy.
sentences.zh: 我们不再欣赏生命中那些了不起的人，也不再珍惜健康的幸运。

sentences.en: We become habituated to these gifts and stop noticing them.
sentences.zh: 我们对这些礼物产生了习惯化，不再注意到它们。

sentences.en: With Cass Sunstein, Tali Sharratt is the co-author of the book, Look Again, The Power of Noticing What Was Always There.
sentences.zh: 塔莉·沙罗特与卡斯·桑斯坦合著了《再看一眼：注意到一直存在的事物的力量》一书。

sentences.en: Tali, so far we've talked mostly about the ways we habituate to positive things.
sentences.zh: 塔莉，到目前为止，我们主要讨论了我们对积极事物产生习惯化的方式。

sentences.en: But of course, the mind also habituates to negative things.
sentences.zh: 但当然，大脑也会对消极事物产生习惯化。

sentences.en: In 1999, a huge public works project in Massachusetts was wrapping up.
sentences.zh: 1999年，马萨诸塞州一个巨大的公共工程项目即将结束。

sentences.en: It had taken a decade to complete.
sentences.zh: 它花了十年时间才完成。

sentences.en: All that remained was to open an underwater tunnel.
sentences.zh: 剩下的唯一工作就是打开一条水下隧道。

sentences.en: I want to play you a public television news clip about what happened that day.
sentences.zh: 我想为你播放一段关于那天发生的事情的公共电视新闻片段。

sentences.en: The tunnel, burrowed into the bay's bedrock, was devoid of light and oxygen,
sentences.zh: 这条挖掘在海湾基岩中的隧道，没有光线和氧气，

sentences.en: requiring the divers to carry a specialized breathing system.
sentences.zh: 要求潜水员携带专门的呼吸系统。

sentences.en: On a July morning, the five divers set out.
sentences.zh: 在一个七月的早晨，五名潜水员出发了。

sentences.en: Disaster struck when the breathing system malfunctioned.
sentences.zh: 当呼吸系统发生故障时，灾难降临了。

sentences.en: Three of the divers made it out alive, but two died.
sentences.zh: 三名潜水员活着出来了，但两人死亡。

sentences.en: 33-year-old William Juice and 39-year-old Tim Nordean died of asphyxiation.
sentences.zh: 33岁的威廉·朱斯和39岁的蒂姆·诺迪恩死于窒息。

sentences.en: Tali, tell me the story of this project and what it tells us about habituation.
sentences.zh: 塔莉，给我讲讲这个项目的故事，以及它告诉我们关于习惯化的什么道理。

sentences.en: So there was a decade-long Boston Harbor cleanup.
sentences.zh: 这是一个长达十年的波士顿港清理工程。

sentences.en: So if you visit Boston today, there's clear blue waters, you know, there's sailing boats all around.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你今天去波士顿，那里有清澈湛蓝的海水，你知道，到处都是帆船。

sentences.en: But back in the day, apparently, it was quite dirty.
sentences.zh: 但在过去，显然，它非常脏。

sentences.en: It wasn't as nice.
sentences.zh: 没那么好。

sentences.en: And so they had hundreds of workers working.
sentences.zh: 所以他们有数百名工人在工作。

sentences.en: It cost $4 billion to clean up the harbor.
sentences.zh: 清理港口花费了40亿美元。

sentences.en: And it was high risk the whole time.
sentences.zh: 而且整个过程风险很高。

sentences.en: But at the very end, they sent five divers into a tube hundreds of feet below the ocean floor to remove heavy safety plugs.
sentences.zh: 但在最后，他们派了五名潜水员进入海底数百英尺深的一根管子里，去拆除沉重的安全塞。

sentences.en: And the tunnel had no oxygen or light.
sentences.zh: 隧道里没有氧气或光线。

sentences.en: And the narrowest part of it was only five feet in diameter.
sentences.zh: 最窄的部分直径只有五英尺。

sentences.en: And the divers were to travel all the way to the far end of the 10-mile-long tunnel.
sentences.zh: 潜水员要一直走到这条10英里长隧道的尽头。

sentences.en: And then inside a series of pipes, there were only about 30 inches wide.
sentences.zh: 而在里面的一系列管道中，宽度只有大约30英寸。

sentences.en: So they became kind of smaller and smaller.
sentences.zh: 所以它们变得越来越小。

sentences.en: And despite the project was pretty complex, the drivers trained for it for only two weeks.
sentences.zh: 尽管这个项目非常复杂，但潜水员只为此训练了两周。

sentences.en: And they relied on experimental breathing apparatus, right?
sentences.zh: 而且他们依赖的是实验性的呼吸装置，对吧？

sentences.en: So it doesn't seem that a lot of cautionary measures were taken.
sentences.zh: 所以看起来并没有采取太多的预防措施。

sentences.en: And unfortunately, the breathing system failed.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，呼吸系统失效了。

sentences.en: And only three of the five divers got back to safety.
sentences.zh: 五名潜水员中只有三名回到了安全地带。

sentences.en: And even those that got back to safety had only 30 seconds to spare.
sentences.zh: 即使是那些回到安全地带的人，也只剩下30秒的时间了。

sentences.en: And so it actually is not unusual that disasters in, for example, these kind of construction projects, they tend to happen very late in the project, towards the very end.
sentences.zh: 所以，例如在这些建筑项目中，灾难往往发生在项目后期，接近尾声时，这其实并不罕见。

sentences.en: Because what seems to happen is that early on, people are very cautious, they're very risk-averse, they take, you know, all the measures.
sentences.zh: 因为似乎发生的情况是，早期人们非常谨慎，非常规避风险，他们采取了，你知道，所有的措施。

sentences.en: But then after time, they habituate to the risk.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，他们对风险产生了习惯化。

sentences.en: They don't have the emotional reaction, the anxiety and the fear.
sentences.zh: 他们没有那种情绪反应，没有焦虑和恐惧。

sentences.en: And that's when most of the accidents on construction sites tend to happen.
sentences.zh: 而这正是建筑工地上大多数事故发生的时候。

sentences.en: So you've conducted research that examines the process of risk habituation using virtual reality.
sentences.zh: 所以你进行了一项研究，利用虚拟现实来考察风险习惯化的过程。

sentences.en: Tell me the setup of these studies, Tali.
sentences.zh: 塔莉，跟我说说这些研究的设置吧。

sentences.en: Right, so we wanted to put people in a really threatening position, something that really will kind of cause them fear.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们想把人们置于一个真正具有威胁性的位置，一些真正会引起他们恐惧的东西。

sentences.en: But of course, we can't put our participants in a place where they're really under physical risk.
sentences.zh: 但当然，我们不能把参与者放在真正有身体危险的地方。

sentences.en: So we use the next best thing, which is virtual reality.
sentences.zh: 所以我们使用了次优选择，也就是虚拟现实。

sentences.en: And we use this game in virtual reality where what you see is yourself going up, an elevator, up, a skyscraper, and then the elevator opens up.
sentences.zh: 我们在虚拟现实中使用了一个游戏，你看到的是自己乘电梯上升，来到摩天大楼顶层，然后电梯门打开。

sentences.en: And then you can walk on a plank that is basically far, far, far up, up, up, up, up.
sentences.zh: 然后你可以走上一块木板，它基本上是在非常、非常、非常高的地方。

sentences.en: And you're looking down and it's really scary.
sentences.zh: 你往下看，真的很吓人。

sentences.en: Now, it absolutely tricks your brain to believe that I'm thousands of feet up walking on a plank.
sentences.zh: 它绝对会欺骗你的大脑，让你相信自己正站在几千英尺高空的木板上行走。

sentences.en: And if I just tip, I'm going to fall and I'm going to die.
sentences.zh: 如果我稍微倾斜一下，我就会掉下去，然后死掉。

sentences.en: It is amazing how that feels so real.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉如此真实，真是太神奇了。

sentences.en: And so what we had is we had our participants go up and they maybe took like one little step.
sentences.zh: 所以我们让参与者走上去，他们可能只迈了一小步。

sentences.en: We asked them, how are you feeling?
sentences.zh: 我们问他们，你感觉怎么样？

sentences.en: And we also measured skin conductance response because when you are anxious, you sweat and skin conductance response goes up.
sentences.zh: 我们还测量了皮肤电导反应，因为当你焦虑时，你会出汗，皮肤电导反应就会上升。

sentences.en: And what we found is at the beginning, they were very anxious and they only took a few steps.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，起初他们非常焦虑，只走了几步。

sentences.en: But over time, people were just jumping off the plank with no anxiety response whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，人们直接从木板上跳了下来，没有任何焦虑反应。

sentences.en: And what was interesting is that those individuals that habituated faster, so it only took them a few times to like not feel any fear or anxiety at all.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，那些习惯化得更快的人，只需要几次尝试，就完全感觉不到任何恐惧或焦虑了。

sentences.en: We had this questionnaire asking them about risk taking in real life, whether it's sports or driving or unsafe sex.
sentences.zh: 我们有一份问卷，询问他们现实生活中的冒险行为，无论是运动、驾驶还是不安全的性行为。

sentences.en: And those people who we could measure that their emotional habituation was really fast, right?
sentences.zh: 而那些我们能测量出情绪习惯化非常快的人，对吧？

sentences.en: Those are the people who really took risks in life.
sentences.zh: 这些人就是生活中真正会冒险的人。

sentences.en: So we've looked at the role of habituation when it comes to risk, but that's not the only domain in which we can see habituation when it comes to negative things.
sentences.zh: 所以我们研究了习惯化在风险方面的作用，但这并不是我们能观察到对负面事物产生习惯化的唯一领域。

sentences.en: You've also looked at habituation when it comes to dishonesty.
sentences.zh: 你也研究过关于不诚实行为的习惯化。

sentences.en: Can you tell me how you've designed those studies?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我你是如何设计这些研究的吗？

sentences.en: What is the setup of those studies?
sentences.zh: 这些研究的设置是什么？

sentences.en: We were interested in whether people habituate to their own lying.
sentences.zh: 我们感兴趣的是人们是否会对自己的撒谎行为产生习惯化。

sentences.en: Most people think that lying is immoral, right?
sentences.zh: 大多数人认为撒谎是不道德的，对吧？

sentences.en: But if your emotional response will go down over time, the more you lie, then you'd probably lie more and more and more.
sentences.zh: 但如果你的情绪反应随着时间的推移而降低，你撒谎越多，你可能就会撒谎得越来越多。

sentences.en: And this is exactly what we tested.
sentences.zh: 而这正是我们所测试的。

sentences.en: So we had people come into the lab and we asked them to play a game.
sentences.zh: 所以我们让人们来到实验室，请他们玩一个游戏。

sentences.en: And in this game, they realized that if they lied to the other person, they could gain more money at the expense of the other person.
sentences.zh: 在这个游戏中，他们意识到如果对另一个人撒谎，他们可以以牺牲对方为代价获得更多的钱。

sentences.en: And we also recorded their brain activity.
sentences.zh: 我们还记录了他们的大脑活动。

sentences.en: And what we found that at the beginning, they liked, but just a little bit, maybe a few cents.
sentences.zh: 我们发现起初他们撒谎了，但只是撒了一点点，可能只有几美分。

sentences.en: Next time they had an opportunity, maybe a few dollars.
sentences.zh: 下一次有机会时，可能就是几美元了。

sentences.en: And the amount by which they lied became bigger and bigger, right?
sentences.zh: 他们撒谎的金额变得越来越大，对吧？

sentences.en: It's like the slippery slope.
sentences.zh: 这就像滑坡效应。

sentences.en: And at the same time, we looked at activity in their amygdala.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，我们观察了他们杏仁核的活动。

sentences.en: So the amygdala is a small part of the brain, and it is important for emotional arousal.
sentences.zh: 杏仁核是大脑中的一个小区域，对情绪唤起很重要。

sentences.en: And what we found is at the beginning when people lied, there was a strong emotional response, right?
sentences.zh: 我们发现起初当人们撒谎时，有强烈的情绪反应，对吧？

sentences.en: They felt bad about lying.
sentences.zh: 他们对撒谎感到难过。

sentences.en: The next time they lied, less of an emotional response.
sentences.zh: 下一次他们撒谎时，情绪反应就变小了。

sentences.en: The third time they lied, less.
sentences.zh: 第三次撒谎时，反应更小了。

sentences.en: And as the amygdala activity went down, indicating less emotional arousal, people lied more and more and more.
sentences.zh: 随着杏仁核活动减弱，表明情绪唤起降低，人们撒谎的次数就越来越多。

sentences.en: That study looks at how we habituate to our own lying, but you also habituate to the lies of other people.
sentences.zh: 那项研究着眼于我们如何对自己撒谎产生习惯化，但你也会对他人的谎言产生习惯化。

sentences.en: If you are in an environment, let's say a work environment, where people are lying, but they start with small lies.
sentences.zh: 如果你身处一个环境，比如工作环境，人们在撒谎，但他们从小的谎言开始。

sentences.en: You know, maybe they lie a little bit about their expenses.
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许他们在报销费用上撒了一点小谎。

sentences.en: You know, maybe they lie a little bit to the client about what the product can do.
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许他们对客户关于产品功能撒了一点小谎。

sentences.en: And then they lie more and more and more.
sentences.zh: 然后他们撒谎越来越多。

sentences.en: They start really taking in, you know, thousands of dollars that they shouldn't.
sentences.zh: 他们开始真正地获取本不该属于他们的数千美元。

sentences.en: You are more likely to just accept and maybe not even notice if the lies are gradual.
sentences.zh: 如果谎言是循序渐进的，你更有可能只是接受，甚至可能根本没有注意到。

sentences.en: And we see this in reality when people who have been quite dishonest, Bernie Madoff, for example,
sentences.zh: 我们在现实中看到了这一点，比如伯纳德·麦道夫这样相当不诚实的人，

sentences.en: they actually tell you about how they started out with small lies and became bigger and bigger.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上会告诉你他们是如何从小的谎言开始，然后变得越来越大的。

sentences.en: There's a wonderful quote by him.
sentences.zh: 他有一句很棒的名言。

sentences.en: He says, it starts out with you taking a little bit, maybe a few hundred, a few thousand.
sentences.zh: 他说，一开始你只是拿一点点，可能几百块，几千块。

sentences.en: You get comfortable with that.
sentences.zh: 你对此习以为常了。

sentences.en: And before you know it, it snowballs into something big.
sentences.zh: 在你意识到之前，它就像滚雪球一样变成了一个大问题。

sentences.en: And what I like about this quote is that he says, you get comfortable with that.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这句话的一点是，他说你对此习以为常了。

sentences.en: What this tells me is that he probably felt bad about it when he began.
sentences.zh: 这告诉我，他刚开始的时候可能对此感到难过。

sentences.en: But over time, habituation, he became comfortable.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，习惯化了，他变得心安理得了。

sentences.en: Then he can lie more and more.
sentences.zh: 然后他就可以撒更多的谎。

sentences.en: So along the same lines, Tali, I'm guessing we can also habituate to other problematic things,
sentences.zh: 那么同样地，塔莉，我猜我们也可以对其他有问题的事情产生习惯化，

sentences.en: things like misinformation or pollution or corruption.
sentences.zh: 比如错误信息、污染或腐败。

sentences.en: You know, if these are things that are all around us all the time, after some time,
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果这些事情一直围绕在我们身边，过了一段时间，

sentences.en: it becomes hard to muster a sense of outrage.
sentences.zh: 就很难再激起一种愤怒感了。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: With misinformation, actually, there's surveys showing that they ask people,
sentences.zh: 关于错误信息，实际上有调查显示，他们问人们，

sentences.en: do you think it's okay to kind of fudge a story in order to get more clicks?
sentences.zh: 你认为为了获得更多点击量而歪曲事实是可以的吗？

sentences.en: And the percentage of people who said it was okay was much smaller about 15 years ago than it is today.
sentences.zh: 认为这没问题的人所占的比例在15年前比今天小得多。

sentences.en: So I think with all this kind of like fake news and misinformation online, social media,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为随着网上、社交媒体上所有这些假新闻和错误信息，

sentences.en: we started becoming just used to this.
sentences.zh: 我们开始习惯了这一切。

sentences.en: We're not as outraged when we learn that someone is changing the story a little bit
sentences.zh: 当我们得知有人稍微改变了故事，

sentences.en: or maybe just making it up completely.
sentences.zh: 或者可能完全是编造的时候，我们不再那么愤怒了。

sentences.en: It seems that we accept it.
sentences.zh: 似乎我们接受了它。

sentences.en: And we don't have much of an emotional response.
sentences.zh: 而且我们没有太多的情绪反应。

sentences.en: And probably we don't notice it as much.
sentences.zh: 而且我们可能也没有那么注意到它。

sentences.en: So, you know, we've looked at sort of many examples of habituation here when it comes to risk,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们在这里看了很多关于习惯化的例子，涉及风险、

sentences.en: to, you know, misinformation, to dishonesty.
sentences.zh: 你知道，错误信息，不诚实行为。

sentences.en: But at a grand level, I'm also wondering whether it works at the level of society.
sentences.zh: 但在宏观层面上，我也想知道它是否在社会层面也起作用。

sentences.en: So when you look at the rise of authoritarian states, for example,
sentences.zh: 所以当你观察威权国家的兴起时，例如，

sentences.en: you know, sometimes they take away the rights of minorities,
sentences.zh: 你知道，有时他们会剥夺少数群体的权利，

sentences.en: but they don't do everything on day one.
sentences.zh: 但他们不会在第一天就做所有事情。

sentences.en: On day one, it's just a little bit.
sentences.zh: 第一天，只是一点点。

sentences.en: On day 10, it's a little more.
sentences.zh: 第10天，多了一点。

sentences.en: And then by day 500, you know, they've taken away a lot.
sentences.zh: 然后到了第500天，你知道，他们已经剥夺了很多。

sentences.en: But by that point, people have become desensitized
sentences.zh: 但到那时，人们已经变得麻木了，

sentences.en: through the same process of habituation.
sentences.zh: 通过同样的习惯化过程。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Now, I think when we look back at the history of humanity,
sentences.zh: 现在，我认为当我们回顾人类历史时，

sentences.en: there are all these dark stories of oppression and bloody wars and genocide.
sentences.zh: 有所有这些关于压迫、血腥战争和种族灭绝的黑暗故事。

sentences.en: And we often look back and we said, how could that be, right?
sentences.zh: 我们经常回顾过去并说，怎么会这样呢，对吧？

sentences.en: Why wasn't that stopped earlier?
sentences.zh: 为什么没有早点阻止它？

sentences.en: And I think part of the answer is that these extreme political movements
sentences.zh: 我认为部分答案是，这些极端的政治运动

sentences.en: and deadly conflicts, they start small and then they increase gradually.
sentences.zh: 和致命的冲突，它们从小事开始，然后逐渐增加。

sentences.en: And because they increase very gradually, they end up eliciting a weaker emotional reaction.
sentences.zh: 因为它们增加得非常缓慢，最终引发的情绪反应就较弱。

sentences.en: And because there's less emotional reaction, there's less resistance, right?
sentences.zh: 因为情绪反应较少，所以阻力也较小，对吧？

sentences.en: And more acceptance than there would otherwise be.
sentences.zh: 而且比原本的情况有更多的接受度。

sentences.en: And we talk about this in our book and we take Nazi Germany as an example.
sentences.zh: 我们在书中谈到了这一点，并以纳粹德国为例。

sentences.en: And there's a lot of testimonies of, for example, German citizens that explain what happened.
sentences.zh: 有很多证词，例如德国公民解释了发生了什么。

sentences.en: And when you kind of read those testimonies, they often talk about how things really escalated slowly, right?
sentences.zh: 当你阅读这些证词时，他们经常谈论事情是如何缓慢升级的，对吧？

sentences.en: People say that each act and each occasion was worse than the last, but only by a little bit, right?
sentences.zh: 人们说每一个行为和每一个场合都比上一个更糟，但只是一点点，对吧？

sentences.en: So we started by Jews are not allowed to be doctors, not allowed to be journalists,
sentences.zh: 所以我们从犹太人不允许当医生、不允许当记者开始，

sentences.en: then books are burned.
sentences.zh: 然后焚书。

sentences.en: And then, you know, there are hundreds and hundreds of steps.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，有成百上千个步骤。

sentences.en: And the last one is mass murder, is genocide, right?
sentences.zh: 最后一步是大规模屠杀，是种族灭绝，对吧？

sentences.en: If the last act was a first act, that would, I believe, would have resulted in much more of a reaction from the people.
sentences.zh: 如果最后一个行为是第一个行为，我相信，那会引起人们更多的反应。

sentences.en: But it's not.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: And there's this quote from a German citizen that he says that people could not see it developing from day to day,
sentences.zh: 有一位德国公民的名言，他说人们无法看到它日复一日的发展，

sentences.en: like a farmer in the field that doesn't see the corn growing, right?
sentences.zh: 就像田里的农民看不到玉米生长一样，对吧？

sentences.en: It grows slowly, slowly, and then one day it's over your head.
sentences.zh: 它慢慢地生长，然后有一天它就长到你的头顶了。

sentences.en: There are many other scenarios in which our tendency to habituate to bad things can bring terrible consequences.
sentences.zh: 还有许多其他场景，我们对坏事产生习惯化的倾向会带来可怕的后果。

sentences.en: One example, climate change.
sentences.zh: 一个例子，气候变化。

sentences.en: Many of the warning signs of climate change are subtle and easy to miss.
sentences.zh: 气候变化的许多警告信号都很微妙，很容易被忽略。

sentences.en: But even when they are stark and dramatic, think of melting ice caps or raging wildfires or dramatic flooding,
sentences.zh: 但即使当它们变得鲜明而剧烈时，想想冰盖融化、肆虐的野火或剧烈的洪水，

sentences.en: our minds habituate to these phenomena.
sentences.zh: 我们的思想也会对这些现象产生习惯化。

sentences.en: They become expected, normalized.
sentences.zh: 它们变得习以为常，正常化了。

sentences.en: Yeah, so the problem here is that, first of all, perceptually we habituate, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，所以这里的问题是，首先，在感知上我们产生了习惯化，对吧？

sentences.en: When things, let's say pollution, if there's pollution in the air constantly, we kind of get used to it and we don't really notice it's in the air.
sentences.zh: 当事物，比如污染，如果空气中持续有污染，我们就会习惯它，并没有真正注意到它在空气中。

sentences.en: There's a really interesting survey that shows that in the UK, only 10% of people rate their air quality as poor,
sentences.zh: 有一个非常有趣的调查显示，在英国，只有10%的人认为他们的空气质量很差，

sentences.en: despite the fact that pollution breaches legal limits in 88% of UK regions.
sentences.zh: 尽管事实上88%的英国地区污染超过了法律限制。

sentences.en: So, and then there's also just kind of more of accepting of this idea, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，然后还有更多对这个想法的接受，对吧？

sentences.en: Over time, we accept the idea that there's climate change and that there are going to be hurricanes or things like that.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，我们接受了气候变化以及会有飓风之类的事情的想法。

sentences.en: And so we have less of a reaction to it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们对它的反应就变少了。

sentences.en: And in fact, that's also been shown nicely on Twitter.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这在推特上也得到了很好的证明。

sentences.en: So there's a study where they looked at people, what they said about extreme climate events on Twitter.
sentences.zh: 有一项研究观察了人们在推特上对极端气候事件的言论。

sentences.en: What they found is that extreme climate events like hurricanes, for example, as they became more and more frequent, people stopped tweeting about it.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，像飓风这样的极端气候事件，随着它们变得越来越频繁，人们停止了在推特上谈论它。

sentences.en: And on average, it took between two to eight years for people to stop tweeting about climate events like extreme temperature.
sentences.zh: 平均而言，人们停止在推特上谈论极端温度等气候事件需要两到八年的时间。

sentences.en: And if you don't see it and you don't talk about it, then you don't act.
sentences.zh: 如果你看不到它，也不谈论它，那么你就不会采取行动。

sentences.en: So what is the solution for this, Tali?
sentences.zh: 那么塔莉，这个问题的解决方案是什么？

sentences.en: I understand how habituation can work with climate change, but is there a way to fight it?
sentences.zh: 我明白习惯化如何影响气候变化，但有什么方法可以对抗它吗？

sentences.en: Well, I think the solution here is not to rely on our perception, to rely on instruments, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这里的解决方案不是依赖我们的感知，而是依赖仪器，对吧？

sentences.en: The instruments can tell us quite well what is happening with the temperature, with climate events.
sentences.zh: 仪器可以很好地告诉我们温度、气候事件正在发生什么。

sentences.en: And we need to rely on the data, not on our feelings or how we perceive the world to be.
sentences.zh: 我们需要依赖数据，而不是我们的感觉或我们感知世界的方式。

sentences.en: It's just not reliable.
sentences.zh: 那根本不可靠。

sentences.en: Because, of course, I think what you're pointing out is that our perceptions might habituate to climate change, but our instruments will not.
sentences.zh: 因为当然，我认为你指出的正是我们的感知可能会对气候变化产生习惯化，但我们的仪器不会。

sentences.en: And they will continue to tell us the story.
sentences.zh: 它们将继续告诉我们事实。

sentences.en: And if we can't trust our own intuitions, what we can trust is the data coming in from our instruments.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不能相信自己的直觉，我们可以相信的是来自仪器的数据。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But, you know, it's really hard for people to do that.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，人们真的很难做到这一点。

sentences.en: It's really hard for us to say, I'm going to ignore my perception.
sentences.zh: 我们真的很难说，我要忽略我的感知。

sentences.en: I'm going to rely on the instrument.
sentences.zh: 我要依赖仪器。

sentences.en: This is a well-known problem.
sentences.zh: 这是一个众所周知的问题。

sentences.en: Often pilots are flying and they can go into vertigo and they feel like they're flying up towards, you know, up in the air, when in fact they're flying down towards the ground.
sentences.zh: 飞行员在飞行时经常会产生眩晕感，他们感觉自己是在向空中飞行，而实际上他们是在向地面俯冲。

sentences.en: And the instruments show them you're flying down towards the ground, but they feel like they're flying up.
sentences.zh: 仪器显示他们正在向地面俯冲，但他们感觉自己是在向上飞。

sentences.en: And it's really hard to just say, okay, I'm going to go with the instrument, right?
sentences.zh: 真的很难说，好吧，我要相信仪器，对吧？

sentences.en: I'm going to fly my plane into what I believe is into the ground because the instrument is telling me, no, this is the way you should do it.
sentences.zh: 我要把飞机飞向我认为是地面的地方，因为仪器告诉我，不，这才是你应该做的。

sentences.en: And that can lead to accidents and it has led to accidents.
sentences.zh: 这可能导致事故，而且确实已经导致了事故。

sentences.en: I mean,
sentences.zh: 我是说，

sentences.en: so much of the story is about how our brains have this propensity to forget and ignore and eventually not notice something and how in some ways this can be functional in some elements of our lives.
sentences.zh: 这个故事很大程度上是关于我们的大脑如何有这种遗忘、忽略并最终不注意某事的倾向，以及在某种程度上这在我们的生活中某些方面可能是功能性的。

sentences.en: But in other situations, it really is helpful to be able to slow down, to be able to see again.
sentences.zh: 但在其他情况下，能够慢下来，能够再次看清事实确实很有帮助。

sentences.en: And there's not sort of a one-size-fits-all rule when it comes to habituation and dishabituation, is there?
sentences.zh: 关于习惯化和去习惯化，并没有所谓的万能法则，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, on one hand, we all want to kind of have that joy again of the things that have been around us for a long time.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，一方面，我们都想重新找回那些长期陪伴在我们身边的事物所带来的快乐。

sentences.en: And we can remember in the past how much joy they had triggered in us, but now we habituated.
sentences.zh: 我们记得过去它们曾带给我们多少快乐，但现在我们已经习惯了。

sentences.en: So, you know, we want to do these things that can maybe cause us to feel more of the happiness and the joy,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们想要做一些事情，或许能让我们感受到更多的幸福和快乐，

sentences.en: but also to be able to see things around us like cracks in our relationships, inefficiencies at work, but also the bigger things, racism and sexism, so we can act to change them.
sentences.zh: 但同时也能让我们看清周围的事物，比如人际关系中的裂痕、工作中的低效，以及更重大的问题，如种族歧视和性别歧视，这样我们才能采取行动去改变它们。

sentences.en: Tali Sharratt is a cognitive neuroscientist at University College London.
sentences.zh: 塔莉·沙罗特（Tali Sharratt）是伦敦大学学院的认知神经科学家。

sentences.en: Along with Cass Sunstein, she's the author of Look Again, The Power of Noticing What Was Always There.
sentences.zh: 她与卡斯·桑斯坦（Cass Sunstein）合著了《再看一眼：察觉常在之物的力量》（Look Again, The Power of Noticing What Was Always There）一书。
